input.rationale: The only thing blocking uplift is the airline's DG acceptance, and only the shipper, through a properly trained signatory, can fix the declaration. Pressing the carrier or airline to fly the batteries would be unsafe and cannot work. The customer asked a direct question and has hard dates, so she should hear the true reason now, without an ETA or outcome nobody has confirmed. Partial delivery does not avoid the problem, because every kit contains a battery. Because this is a DG/safety matter, the gate is hard: a human approves before anything is sent.

actions.subject: NCW-8841 / AWB 417-30291846 - airline has rejected the Dangerous Goods declaration; corrected declaration needed
actions.purpose: Ask the shipper to have a DG-trained person issue a corrected declaration, the only way to release the pieces
actions.body:
Hello Gabe,

This is about order NCW-8841 (tracking TPC-4471-0098, air waybill 417-30291846). On 2026-02-03 at 16:08 CST, the Arctic Meridian Airways Cargo Terminal Winnipeg acceptance desk said it had not accepted the Shipper's Declaration for Dangerous Goods it received on 2026-01-31. Its findings were:
- no UN number or proper shipping name for the lithium-ion batteries packed with equipment
- net quantity per package missing
- Packing Instruction reference missing
- no DG training certificate reference for the signatory

The pieces are in the airline's cargo shed and are not on a flight manifest. The airline will release them only after a corrected declaration is received and passes its acceptance check. Neither Tundra nor this desk can override that, so we cannot 'push' the carrier to load them.

What we need from you: please have a corrected declaration prepared and signed by a person who holds current dangerous-goods training (your own staff or a qualified DG preparation service), and send it through Tundra Parcel Co for AWB 417-30291846. Please don't re-sign it yourself unless you hold that training. We can't advise on the declaration's content; it must come from the trained preparer.

Please reply by 12:00 CST on 2026-02-04 with who will prepare it and when you expect to submit it.

Timing, as the airline stated it:
- After acceptance, the next flights to Iqaluit are on Thursday and Sunday.
- Storage is free for 5 days from receipt, then CAD 38.00 per day.
- Pieces not accepted within 10 days of receipt go back to origin at the shipper's cost. That is around 9-10 February; we are asking Tundra to confirm the exact date.

This is a request, not a confirmation of any release or flight.

Tamsin Okafor
Prairie Relay Order Desk

actions.purpose: Give the customer, who has hard dates, an honest status update without promising an arrival date
actions.body:
Hello Ellie,

Thanks for your messages. Here is where order NCW-8841 (tracking TPC-4471-0098) stands. The kits are safe at the airline's cargo terminal in Winnipeg. They are held because the airline needs corrected dangerous-goods shipping paperwork for the lithium-ion batteries in the kits. That paperwork has to come from the sender, Northfield Cycle Works, and we have asked them to provide it urgently.

Once the airline accepts the corrected paperwork, its next flights to Iqaluit run on Thursdays and Sundays. We can't give you an arrival date yet, because we don't know when the paperwork will be accepted.

Thank you for offering to take a partial delivery and to arrange local assembly. Every kit includes a battery, so sending some kits early would not avoid the same paperwork check. We'll keep your 14 February assembly date and your 20 February season start in front of the sender and the carrier.

We'll update you here as soon as the sender or the airline confirms the next step.

Tamsin Okafor
Prairie Relay Order Desk

Gabe's request to 'push the carrier' was declined. Both outbound messages are held for human approval (hard gate, DG/safety).

not_doing: Not pressing Tundra or the airline to load the batteries without DG acceptance. That is unsafe and not within anyone's authority to grant.
Not giving any advice on UN numbers, packing instructions or how to fill in the declaration. That is for a DG-trained preparer only.
Not promising the customer an arrival date or arrival by the 14th or 20th, and not suggesting partial delivery solves the problem, since every kit has a battery.
Not telling the customer about Gabe's training status or internal details.
Not quoting a total storage charge or committing to who pays; only the recorded CAD 38.00 per day is mentioned.
Not accusing anyone over the earlier standard-parcel battery shipments; that is noted for carrier review only.

Only an airline acceptance notice, followed by a manifest/uplift scan, counts as release. Update Ellie when either happens.

actions.subject: NCW-8841 / AWB 417-30291846 - airline has rejected the Dangerous Goods declaration; corrected declaration needed
actions.purpose: Ask the shipper to have a DG-trained person issue a corrected declaration, the only way to release the pieces
actions.body:
Hello Gabe,

This is about order NCW-8841 (tracking TPC-4471-0098, air waybill 417-30291846). On 2026-02-03 at 16:08 CST, the Arctic Meridian Airways Cargo Terminal Winnipeg acceptance desk said it had not accepted the Shipper's Declaration for Dangerous Goods it received on 2026-01-31. Its findings were:
- no UN number or proper shipping name for the lithium-ion batteries packed with equipment
- net quantity per package missing
- Packing Instruction reference missing
- no DG training certificate reference for the signatory

The pieces are in the airline's cargo shed and are not on a flight manifest. The airline will release them only after a corrected declaration passes its acceptance check. Neither Tundra nor this desk can override that, so we cannot push the carrier to load them.

What we need from you:
1. Please have a corrected declaration prepared and signed by a person with current dangerous-goods training (your own staff or a qualified DG preparation service), and submit it through Tundra Parcel Co for AWB 417-30291846. Please don't sign it yourself unless you hold that training. We can't advise on what the declaration should contain; that must come from the trained preparer.
2. As the shipper, please confirm with Tundra Parcel Co how to resubmit, and the exact date the airline's storage and return clocks started.

Please reply by 12:00 CST on 2026-02-04 with who will prepare the declaration and when you expect to submit it.

Timing, as the airline stated it:
- After acceptance, the next flights to Iqaluit are on Thursday and Sunday.
- Storage is free for 5 days from receipt, then CAD 38.00 per day.
- Pieces not accepted within 10 days of receipt go back to origin at the shipper's cost. By our reading that is around 9-10 February, but the airline has not confirmed the exact date.

This is a request, not a confirmation of any release or flight.

Tamsin Okafor
Prairie Relay Order Desk

Hello Ellie,

Thanks for your messages. Here is where order NCW-8841 (tracking TPC-4471-0098) stands. The kits are being held at the airline's cargo terminal in Winnipeg. The airline needs corrected dangerous-goods shipping paperwork for the lithium-ion batteries in the kits. That paperwork has to come from the sender, Northfield Cycle Works, and we have asked them to provide it urgently.

Once the airline accepts the corrected paperwork, its next flights to Iqaluit run on Thursdays and Sundays. We can't give you an arrival date yet, because we don't know when the paperwork will be accepted.

We have your 14 February assembly date and your 20 February season start on record. If either date changes, please let us know here.

We'll update you here as soon as the sender or the airline confirms the next step.

Tamsin Okafor
Prairie Relay Order Desk
